==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|pā|a=RP,GA}}, {{IPA|en|/peɪ/|[pʰeɪ̯]}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-pay.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪ|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=give money|:inh|enm:payen|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|payen}}, from {{der|en|fro|paiier||pay}}, from {{der|en|la-med|pācāre||to settle, satisfy}} from {{der|en|la|pācō|pācāre|to pacify}}. In this sense, displaced native {{ncog|ang|ġield||pay}} and {{m|ang|ġieldan||to pay}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|yield}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb|+|+|paid,~ed<l:obsolete>}}

# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[give]] [[money]] or other compensation to in exchange for goods or services.
#: {{co|en|'''pay''' cash or '''pay''' in cash, '''pay''' by credit/debit card}}
#: {{co|en|'''pay''' in dollars/euros, etc.}}
#: {{ux|en|How much will the job '''pay'''?}}
#: {{ux|en|She is '''paying''' him to clean the place up.}}
#: {{ux|en|He doesn't have money, but he '''pays''' rent in chores and housework.}}
#: {{ux|en|He was '''paid''' [[off the books]] and [[in kind]] where possible.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=17|passage=This time was most dreadful for Lilian. Thrown on her own resources and almost penniless, she maintained herself and '''paid''' the rent of a wretched room near the hospital by working as a charwoman, sempstress, anything.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-21|author=w:Oliver Burkeman|volume=189|issue=2|page=48|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly|title=[http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google The tao of tech]|passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about{{...}}and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention. Partly, this is a result of how online advertising has traditionally worked: advertisers '''pay''' for clicks, and a click is a click, however it's obtained.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|or|transitive}} To deposit into an account.
#: {{ux|en|I '''pay''' a portion of each paycheck into a savings account.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To discharge, as a debt or other obligation, by giving or doing what is due or required.
#: {{syn|en|pay off|repay}}
#: {{co|en|to '''pay''' compensation, to '''pay''' a fine}}
#: {{ux|en|She offered to '''pay''' the bill.}}
#: {{ux|en|He is '''paying''' his debt to society.}}
#: {{ux|en|He was allowed to go as soon as the kidnappers were '''paid'''.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Psalms|37|21|passage=The wicked borroweth, and '''payeth''' not again.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Lucrece|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SjYOAQAAMAAJ&pg=PT38|passage=The petty ſtreames that '''paie''' a dailie [[debt|det]] / To their ſalt ſoveraigne with their freſh [[falls|fals]] [[haste|haſt]], / Adde to his flowe, but alter not his [[tast|taſt]].}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=68|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579860-g8-pledges-tackle-three-ts-t-time T time]|passage=Yet in “Through a Latte, Darkly”, a new study of how Starbucks has largely avoided '''paying''' tax in Britain, Edward Kleinbard […] shows that current tax rules make it easy for all sorts of firms to generate what he calls “stateless income”: […]. In Starbucks’s case, the firm has in effect turned the process of making an expensive cup of coffee into intellectual property.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|or|transitive}} To be profitable; to be [[worth it]].
#: {{ux|en|It didn't '''pay''' him to keep the store open any more.}}
#: {{ux|en|Crime doesn’t '''pay'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|It will '''pay''' to wait.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[cover]], as a cost.
#: {{ux|en|Those investments '''paid''' for her college education.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To yield as a benefit.
#: {{syn|en|pay out|yield|return}}
#: {{co|en|to '''pay''' dividends; to '''pay''' interest}}
#: {{ux|en|You will get '''paid''' from this investment yearly.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[give]] (something else than money).
#: {{co|en|to '''pay''' attention, to '''pay''' tribute, to '''pay''' a visit}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Midsummer|V|i|passage=not '''paying''' me a welcome}}
#* {{RQ:Marshall Squire's Daughter|A Court Ball|9|They stayed together during three dances, went out on to the terrace, explored wherever they were permitted to explore, '''paid''' two visits to the buffet, and enjoyed themselves much in the same way as if they had been school-children surreptitiously breaking loose from an assembly of grown-ups.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To suffer [[consequence]]s, especially [[justly]].
#: {{ux|en|He '''paid''' for his fun in the sun with a terrible sunburn.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To admit that a joke, punchline, etc., was [[funny]].

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# [[money|Money]] given in return for [[work]]; [[salary]] or [[wages]].
#: {{ux|en|Many employers have rules designed to keep employees from comparing their '''pays'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=10|passage=The skipper Mr. Cooke had hired at Far Harbor was a God-fearing man with a luke warm interest in his new billet and employer, and had only been prevailed upon to take charge of the yacht after the offer of an emolument equal to half a year's sea '''pay''' of an ensign in the navy.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|rare}} A paying job; a paying concern.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1950|author=Norman Lindsay|authorlink=Norman Lindsay|title={{w|Dust or Polish?}}|publisher=Angus and Robertson|location=Sydney|page=36|passage="You can if you like. I'll drop in each day to see how she gets on." "Oh, will you? That's a relief. All the same, I wouldn't say she was a very good '''pay''', if you spend too much time on her." "Oh, bad '''pays''' make up half a doctor's job."}}
